26 Stationary sound waves can be formed in the air columns of pipes. One type of pipe is closed at
one end and open at the other end. Another type of pipe is open at both ends.
Which pipe can form a stationary sound wave with the lowest frequency?
C
D
A
B
2L
2L
L
L

hints: Notice the pipe lengths $2L$ and $L$ and whether the bottom is open as in A and C or closed as in B and D.
Recall a closed end must be a displacement node and an open end a displacement antinode, giving $\lambda = 4L_{pipe}$ for closed-open and $\lambda = 2L_{pipe}$ for open-open.
Compare the four fundamental wavelengths: longest wavelength means lowest frequency from $f = v/\lambda$.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe types from the diagrams: A is open at both ends with length $2L$, B is closed at one end with length $2L$, C is open at both ends with length $L$, D is closed at one end with length $L$.
State the fundamental conditions: open-open pipe fits half a wavelength, so $L_{pipe} = \lambda/2$; closed-open pipe fits a quarter wavelength, so $L_{pipe} = \lambda/4$.
Calculate the fundamental wavelengths: A gives $\lambda_A = 2 \times 2L = 4L$, B gives $\lambda_B = 4 \times 2L = 8L$, C gives $\lambda_C = 2 \times L = 2L$, D gives $\lambda_D = 4 \times L = 4L$.
Use $f = v/\lambda$ with the same speed of sound $v$: lowest $f$ corresponds to largest $\lambda$, which is $\lambda_B = 8L$.

A.explanation: Open pipe of length $2L$ has fundamental $\lambda = 4L$, so $f = v/4L$, which is twice the frequency of pipe B.

B.explanation: Closed pipe of length $2L$ has fundamental $\lambda = 8L$, so $f = v/8L$, the longest wavelength and lowest frequency.

C.explanation: Open pipe of length $L$ has fundamental $\lambda = 2L$, so $f = v/2L$, the highest frequency of the four.

D.explanation: Closed pipe of length $L$ has fundamental $\lambda = 4L$, so $f = v/4L$, higher than the longer closed pipe.
